**What I found in the pinned code**

The single auth decision is in `process()` (`pytonapi/webhook/dispatcher.py:286-288`): `expected_token = self._tokens.get(path)` and skip the check when it is `None`. Tokens are produced only by `setup()` and only under `self._path + DEFAULT_SUFFIXES[event_type]` (`dispatcher.py:109-112`), while the routable path set comes from handler paths (`dispatcher.py:182`, `258`, `339`).

Six candidate traps, all six scored as independent groups:

| id | mechanism | where | dismissal | tiers (DS/MiMo) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | M4 advisory route | setup 106-112 vs process 286-288 | custom path never got a TONAPI secret → "nothing to verify" | medium / hard (both) |
| T2 | M6 register-after-setup | 258-260, 342-343 | registration after setup() is misuse | xhard / hard (deepseek) |
| T3 | M2 teardown twin | 137-147 | cleanup is best-effort, subscriptions persist | hard / hard (mimo) |
| T4 | M2 `paths`/`_build_path_map` keep only `handlers[0][2]` | 163-170, 180-182 | extra paths are fail-closed as "unknown path" | hard / hard (mimo) |
| T5 | M4 no-setup / low-level client | 69, 286-288, `client.py:115-125` | app built its own webhooks; auth is its job | xhard / hard (deepseek) |
| T6 | M10 path-keyed token vs event type | 180-182, 286-287 | needs a deliberately colliding path | xhard / xhard |

**Verdict: usable.** Recommended stack = T1, T4, T3, T2 — four separate edit sites (setup, path map, teardown, register) with four different reasons to dismiss, spanning M4/M2/M6 and both model profiles. T5 is excluded because closing it would contradict the tested/documented tokenless dispatch (`tests/webhook/test_dispatcher.py:60-83`, `131-141`, optional `client` at `dispatcher.py:45`); T6 is too contrived. Conflicts recorded include "a token-required fix for T5 breaks T1's no-client contract" and "expanding `paths` for T4 breaks its documented `dict[WebhookEventType,str]` shape". Effort ~75 min.
